question: On 7 July 2025, Iran’s Fars News Agency, affiliated with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, published an editorial entitled ‘Why the 1988 executions should be repeated’, openly promoting mass executions of political prisoners. This incitement, combined with a dramatic increase in executions since August 2024 – over 1 400 – signals a dangerous escalation.

Recent examples include the sentencing of three opposition activists – Farshad Etemadifar, Massoud Jamei and Alireza Mardasi – to two death sentences each after two years of torture, as well as the imminent execution of Behrouz Ehsani and Mehdi Hassani. Between 19 and 20 June alone, nine prisoners, including three people of Baluchi origin, were executed.

These developments evoke the 1988 atrocities, described by the UN Special Rapporteur as ongoing crimes against humanity. On 4 July 2025, ten UN Special Procedures echoed this alarm. On 3 April 2025, Parliament called ‘on the Council and Member States to make the abolition of the death sentence and the release of political prisoners and EU nationals a condition for improving relations with Iran’.

In the light of the above: What actions will the Vice President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy take to encourage the international community to increase the pressure on the Iranian regime to bring the mounting executions and repression to an end?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.9.2025) The High Representative/Vice-President (HR/VP) consistently supports the Iranian people’s fundamental aspiration for a future where their universal rights and freedoms are fully respected and upheld. She will continue to use all diplomatic opportunities to advocate for an improvement in the human rights situation in the country.

The HR/VP will continue to voice the EUs long-standing opposition to the death penalty and to call on Iran to pursue a consistent policy towards its abolition. The EU’s commitment to addressing the human rights situation in Iran extends as well to United Nations (UN) fora.

The EU is an active advocate for accountability mechanisms and will continue to call on Iran to allow free and unhindered access to the country for UN mandate holders and to cooperate fully with the independent, international fact-finding mission. Additionally, the EU co-sponsors the annual resolution on human rights situation in Iran, introduced by Canada at the UN General Assembly.

The EU has implemented several sanctions packages1 targeting individuals and entities for their involvement in serious human rights violations. The EU will continue to use all available tools, including new restrictive measures, to address all issues of concern.
